title: introduce-region-affinity-enforcer-and-audit-clarity-adapter
author: Priya Menon
release_notes: Adds region-affinity enforcement at the authorization gateway and enriches audit logs with region provenance and KMS binding verification. No user-facing API changes. Rollout is staged behind a feature flag.
description:
Motivation: We observed two classes of compliance gaps in customer audits: (1) operator/service requests that requested KMS wrapping outside the tenant's declared region, and (2) audit events without a clear, verifiable region provenance field. Both lead to manual investigations during post-incident reviews and increased compliance risk for regulated customers. This PR introduces a lightweight, RBAC-v2-aware "region affinity enforcer" in the authz path and an "audit clarity adapter" that normalizes and signs region provenance into outgoing audit events.

Design summary: - region-affinity-enforcer: middleware in services/authz that validates the incoming claim/headers against tenant-residency policies and the active RBAC v2 policy graph. It rejects or annotates requests based on policy violations and supports a configurable fail-mode (reject | tag-and-allow | warn). - provenance-cache: in-memory LRU cache of recent region-assertions (service principal -> region) to avoid repeated policy evaluation for hot paths; TTL is configurable per deployment. - kms-binding-check: small verification routine that ensures the chosen KMS key is allowed for the asserted region and tenant. This check consults the KMS allowlist and falls back to a safe default when the KMS provider is multi-region but no explicit binding exists. - audit-clarity-adapter: post-processing hook that injects a region_provenance field, kms_binding asserted_by, and a compact signed_digest for non-repudiation into the audit event stream. The adapter also emits structured metrics for policy denials and ambiguous bindings.

Commits (high-level): - 8f3a2d4: add middleware scaffold and interfaces for region assertion evaluation - d1b7a3c: implement RBAC v2 policy lookup and match engine optimizations - e5c92b1: add provenance-cache with LRU and unit tests - 2c7f0d9: implement kms-binding-check and small shim to KMS provider registry - a4b6e77: audit-clarity-adapter + event signing + integration tests - f9d3b11: feature flag, migrations for policy export, and docs updates

Files changed (high level): - services/authz/enforcer.go (new) - services/authz/policy/graph.go (policy resolution tweaks) - services/authz/cache/provenance_lru.go (new) - services/audit/clarity_adapter.go (new) - pkg/kms/validator.go (new helper) - infra/helm/values-production.yaml (feature flag defaults) - docs/security/region-affinity.md (deploy + runbook) - test/integration/region_affinity_test.go (new) - internal/telemetry/metrics_registry.go (new metrics) - web/console/flags/feature_flags.go (UI toggle) - scripts/policy-export-migrate.sh (migration helper)

Behavior and configuration: - Feature flagged under 'region_affinity_enforcer' with rollout percentages supported in console. Default production config: fail-mode=tag-and-allow for 0-25% rollout, reject for 100% rollout after validation window. - Cache defaults: size=4096 entries, TTL=5m. Tunable via helm or private installer. - KMS allowlist consulted via existing kms-provider-config; new optional per-tenant override supported. - Backwards compatibility: when feature flag is off, behavior unchanged. When tag-and-allow is enabled, audit events include a 'policy_warning' tag but requests are allowed.

Review conversation (summarized as a single continuous narrative): Ethan Moreland: "Can we avoid a sync call to the policy store on every request?" — Priya: "Implemented a provenance cache (LRU) and added metrics for cache hit/miss; lookups now limited to cold misses." Sofia Alvarez: "Audit events need a compact signature but not full cryptographic overhead on the hot path." — Priya: "Adapter signs only the digest using a rotating HMAC key; verification path is available in the audit consumer. We kept signing cheap and optional via 'audit_signing' flag." Liam Chen: "What about operator-level overrides for emergency ops?" — Priya: "We added an operator_exemption role template in RBAC v2 with a short-lived TTL; exemptions are audited and emit a metric and event." QA (Maya Singh): "Integration test failing intermittently on CI (TestRegionAffinity/flake)" — Priya: "Tracked to a timing assumption in the test harness; increased test timeouts and added retry logic. CI run: first attempt showed one flaky integration failure; rerun green."

CI and checks: - unit: pass - integration: pass (after rerun) - lint: pass - policy-linter: pass (small rule two warnings addressed) - perf-canary: observed +1.2ms median on authz hot path with cache enabled; documented in PR notes and added an opt-out for low-latency tiers.

Rollout plan: 1) Canary (tag-and-allow) 0-5% for 48h, monitor metrics: policy_denials, policy_warnings, audit_signing_error_rate, authz_latency_p50/p95 2) Expand to 25% tag-and-allow for 72h 3) If stable, flip to reject for remaining 100% behind a scheduled maintenance window. 4) Post-rollout: run policy-export-migrate.sh for policy analytics ingestion and reconcile any tenant-level overrides. Rollback is the feature flag toggle.

Operational runbook (brief): - If policy_denials spike: check policy-graph telemetry and policy-export mismatch; use 'policy-sim' tool to simulate requests. - If audit_signing_error_rate > 0.5%: disable audit_signing flag and check kms-provider HMAC key rotation logs. - If authz latency breach: increase provenance cache size or lower cache TTL depending on workload profile.

Merge: squashed and merged by Sofia Alvarez after approvals and green CI. Changelog and docs updated; internal runbook added under docs/security.

Why this is different: rather than only enforcing direct KMS-region ties, this change focuses on (a) adding a resilient, cache-driven region assertion layer for RBAC v2 decisions, and (b) improving audit signal quality for non-repudiation without imposing heavy crypto costs on the hot path. The approach aims to reduce manual compliance overhead while keeping latency impact minimal.

Notes and follow-ups: - Follow-up ticket ENG-7421: add end-to-end verifier in the audit pipeline consumer to validate signed digests. - Follow-up ticket ENG-7422: UI work to expose per-tenant KMS-binding diagnostics in the console. - Ops note: coordinate with cloud infra to ensure KMS provider registry has up-to-date region metadata before enabling reject mode nationwide.
notes: Feature-flagged rollout; small p50 hit with cache enabled; audit signing is optional to reduce overhead
security_impact: moderate (policy enforcement affects request acceptance) - mitigated via staged rollout and tag-and-allow mode
testing_summary: Unit tests cover policy matching and cache; integration tests validate end-to-end enforcement and audit enrichment; CI required one rerun due to an intermittent harness timeout which was fixed.
